column1: # The seven documents of the measured record, and the arms it records for them.
# `docs/json-pipeline-performance.md` §2 names these seven, §5 records the
# decision each document's class selects, and §3 records the P2 ratio the
# measured pipeline reached against simdjson On-Demand.  This file is the
# corpus the reference arm reads: a row names the document, the arm the
# recorded decision table selects for it on each core class, the documented
# ratio to compare against, and the bytes' digest.
# The bytes live outside the checkout, as §15.49 of the plan records (the
# corpus is the standard document set, not a fixture of this tree).  A digest
# is what makes an outside file one document rather than whatever is there
# today: the arm refuses a file whose digest differs, and names the row when a
# document is absent.  `canada`, `citm` and `twitter` are the 64-byte-aligned
# copies the measurements read; the other four are the generated documents.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   name      the record's name for the document
#   arm_E     the arm on the E-core class (CPUID.1Ah.EAX[31:24] = 0x20)
#   arm_P     the arm on the P-core class (CPUID.1Ah.EAX[31:24] = 0x40)
#   record_E  the record's P2 ratio on the E-core (this pipeline / On-Demand)
#   record_P  the record's P2 ratio on the P-core
#   sha256    the document bytes' digest
#   path      where the document is read from
# An arm is the caller's selector `pipeline.h` documents, not a classifier:
# bit 0 selects B8 (set) or POS8, bit 1 builds the escape list, bit 2 makes the
# UTF-8 stage ungated.  The record's decision table is the selector's
# parameter; `paired.sh --unit reference` prints the arm beside every row.
